newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends mixed as investors bid up yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends mixed as investors bid up yen.

text.p: The dollar ended lower against the Japanese yen Monday on selling ahead of a key Japanese economic report but edged higher against most other major currencies.

Investors began selling dollars for yen in overnight trading, extending losses from Friday. The dollar's slide continued in New York trading before bargain-hunters emerged to bolster the currency, dealers said.

Investors appeared reluctant to hold dollars ahead of the Wednesday's release of Japan's Tankin economic report from major companies. Some investors feared a strong report could increase the chances that Japan will soon raise interest rates.
Higher interest rates in Japan would make securities priced in yen relatively more attractive compared with investments denominated in other currencies.

"It would cause a lot of movement in (the dollar versus the yen) if people thought Japan would raise rates. Then you would see some excitement," said John Hazelton, chief currency dealer at Manufacturers and Traders Bank.
Late Monday, the dollar stood at 107.65 yen, versus 108.15 yen late Friday. The dollar ended slightly higher against the German mark at 1.4790, up from 1.4780.
The yen also climbed against the mark, bolstered by a large buy order from a speculative investor in New York, dealers said.
"One player sold dollars for yen and marks for yen," said Tadatoshi Taso, chief foreign exchange dealer at Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi.
Few observers expect the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates imminently, but any surprising strength in the Tankan could stimulate further yen buying.
"The Bank of Japan will not move as a result of the Tankan, but if the report is (stronger) than expected, the market may move," Taso said.
Selling of marks against the yen also fuelled a smattering of buying of dollars against the mark, and the dollar crawled higher after U.S. trading began.
"The dollar seemed to rebound against the mark. People may have been doing some bargain-hunting," said Jay Wertheimer, senior foreign exchange trader at Banco di Sicilia.

Relatively thin trading may have helped exaggerate the day's price movements, dealers said. A holiday closed markets in London, and many U.S. investors and dealers have scheduled vacations this week ahead of the Labour Day holiday next Monday.
"The day was pretty uneventful. We stayed in a range back and forth in New York and there was very little to get excited about," said Hazelton.
Dealers noted the dollar failed to break through technical resistance at 1.48 marks, its high for the session. Key technical support at 107.50 yen held as the day's low.
In other trade, the dollar rose to 1.1934 Swiss francs from 1.1930 late Friday. The British pound rose to $1.5575 from $1.5565.
The dollar ended unchanged at Canadian $1.3708.
